conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee, one of your surgical team doctors. We're admitting you today for that non-healing ulcer on your left foot. Do you have any questions so far?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. Yes, I’ve been worried. Last time I was here, I got pneumonia and couldn’t have the procedure. Is it safe to do it now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a great question. We reviewed your recent chest X-ray from earlier today. There’s clear improvement in the pneumonia. Your cough has mostly resolved, and you haven’t had fevers. So yes, we feel it’s safe to proceed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. What exactly will you be doing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll do an angiogram to look at the blood flow in your left leg. Then, we plan to place a stent in the popliteal artery behind your knee to improve circulation to your foot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the ulcer? Will that heal better after?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Better blood flow helps wounds heal. We’ll keep up with daily dressing changes, and you’ll continue the collagenase ointment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my transplant meds? I increased my tacrolimus to 2 mg twice a day after last discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve noted that. Transplant nephrology is involved, and we’ll check your tacrolimus levels every morning to keep it in the right range.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve also had some diarrhea off and on. Should I restart the loperamide?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor that. Since it’s not happening now, we won’t restart it yet. But if it returns, we can.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. And my heart? I know I have the mechanical valve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re managing your anticoagulation carefully. You’re on IV heparin now. Before the procedure, we’ll check your INR. If it’s too high, we may give fresh frozen plasma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember that from last time. And after the stent, I’ll need both aspirin and coumadin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. That helps keep the stent open. You’ll continue both long-term.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And when will the procedure happen?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Tomorrow morning. Today, we’ll do some final checks, including another set of labs and your dialysis session.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had dialysis earlier today. Is that okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect timing. That helps us optimize your labs before surgery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my foot still feels very sensitive, even though I don’t have pain. Is that normal?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, with your history of diabetes and neuropathy, that’s common. We’ll keep protecting the area and checking pulses daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs look stable. The PTT is therapeutic at 70.7, so we’ll continue the heparin at 800 units per hour.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my INR? I know it was high last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR was elevated, so we gave two units of fresh frozen plasma this morning. That should help bring it down before the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’m ready when you are.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, we’re back from the procedure. Everything went well. We placed a Zilver stent in your left popliteal artery and used a spider filter during the procedure to catch any debris.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Did the blood flow improve?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the angiogram showed good flow after stenting. Your left foot has dopplerable pulses and is warm, which is a good sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the groin site? Any issues?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We closed the access site with a Perclose device. No bleeding, and we’ll keep an eye on it for hematoma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel a bit tired. Is that normal?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. You’ll rest here for a few hours. We’ll keep you on IV fluids and restart your coumadin tonight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the heparin will continue?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll restart the IV heparin at 800 units per hour tonight and continue it until your INR is therapeutic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re doing well. Your PTT is now 74.2, which is in the therapeutic range. We’ll discharge you today to extended care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: To rehab? Will they manage my heparin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they’ll continue the IV heparin until your INR reaches the goal. You’ll keep taking aspirin and coumadin daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my foot? Should I keep it elevated?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, elevate it above heart level when sitting. Avoid standing too long. And no heavy lifting for a week to protect the groin site.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: When should I call the office?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you have new pain, coldness, or numbness in your leg, a fever over 101.5, or any bleeding from the groin. And keep up with your wound care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. You did great. We’ll see you in follow-up in four weeks.
